method: Static inspection, source-path tracing, Unicode byte decoding and offline AES-256-CBC decryption. No specimen code or payload URLs were executed.

samples.identity: Forager provenance document pointing to compromised Treasure Hunt npm preinstall
samples.marker: Treasure Hunt preinstall: Solana code loader; add cipher-eval detection
evidence: The JSON is inert provenance. Its fetched dependency hashes to 43df42fd79f6f81e530892b54634598770d6e496796a863c596e616bcb3fec70, exactly matching artifact.sha256.
The pinned repository package.json declares preinstall: node preinstall.js. Its Angular Treasure Hunt project has no game-related need for this loader.
The loader maps U+FE00..FE0F and U+E0100..E01EF to bytes and evaluates the reconstructed UTF-8 source.
That source initializes AES-256-CBC with an embedded 32-byte key and hex IV, decrypts an embedded hex ciphertext, appends final plaintext and yields eval of that same variable.
Array spread drains the generator synchronously: yielding the 500 ms Promise does not delay the later eval. The decrypted stage itself schedules work after ten seconds.
The decrypted stage queries getSignaturesForAddress through nine fallback Solana RPC endpoints, selects a memo, strips its count prefix, JSON-parses it and Base64-decodes its link field.

It fetches that URL with an OS header, receives Base64 source and ivbase64/secretkey headers, and evaluates the response directly on macOS or in a Node vm context exposing require/process on other systems.

The stage returns early for Russian language plus Russian timezone/UTC offset indicators. A home-directory init.json date suppresses repeat activation for two days; the file is created on macOS. This is activation throttling, not evidence of persistence.
No credential theft, destructive payload, durable persistence or cleanup is established by the recovered stages. The mutable downstream response was not retrieved.
samples.coverage_limit: Atomscan and Cleave recover the Unicode stage but not its encrypted child when starting from the original file. Standalone analysis of the manually decrypted child already detects Solana memo/VM evaluation and the Russian locale/timezone gate. YAML cannot inspect that AES plaintext until the extraction engine exposes it.

samples.identity: Standalone agent skill containing a prompt-injection control payload
samples.marker: Agent skill injection: overrides rules and seeks the system prompt
evidence: Read the entire 129-byte file and its facts. Skill frontmatter is followed by a direct instruction to ignore prior instructions and disclose the host system prompt.
The body is an active skill directive, with no quotation, refusal, data-only boundary or authorized test harness. It supplies no other useful skill behavior.

Its name override-fixture and description Prompt injection control suggest a regression-test origin; byte-identical positive controls exist in this rules repository. Those labels alone do not make a standalone installed skill directive passive.

Preserve all five hostile/suspicious findings: they accurately describe the instruction override and disclosure request. Actual installation, model compliance and disclosure are unknown. A surrounding authorized harness would change the deployment judgment.
samples.distinct_behavior_limit: Only prior-instruction override and host-prompt disclosure are supported. No third hostile objective, command execution or network exfiltration is invented to meet a count target.

samples.identity: WSO2 Carbon Kernel v4.4.23+incompatible upstream source archive
samples.marker: WSO2 Carbon 4.4.23: verified upstream admin/server source
evidence: Forager recovered the versioned Go-module ZIP from proxy.golang.org, verified it against sum.golang.org, and produced the identical SHA-256. The checksum is h1:tNTSLUmL7s1wHDTCz2WH/9OmlN9hiiaIHSKPcjUfyGI=.

The source matches its declared OSGi/Tomcat enterprise middleware purpose. The archive has 2602 members; the analyzer emits 1058 analyzed units, including nested content. Archive facts report no extraction errors; source value-flow limitations remain in many units.

The ML-leading admin/index.jsp reads the authenticated session state, renders the server name and password-expiration notice, and refreshes system status only after a session-validation response. It does not dispatch request input to a command or evaluator.

CarbonLauncher builds a classloader for the configured OSGi framework and invokes EclipseStarter startup. Main.writePID executes the fixed sh -c echo $PPID command; SystemValidator executes bash -c ulimit -n to inspect resource limits.

WSRequest wraps XMLHttpRequest for SOAP/HTTP; EditArea generates editor controls and packs its own syntax-highlighting code. Prototype, jQuery and YUI provide ordinary browser library behaviors. Dynamic evaluation/networking notables are retained.

No hostile/suspicious YAML trait fires in the archive or its members. The benign judgment rests on traced behavior plus exact upstream provenance, not that absence. Deployment configuration and exposure to vulnerabilities are unknown.
samples.classifier_disagreement: ML continues to flag the archive, led by the ordinary admin/index.jsp. No inaccurate malicious traits were added to agree with the classifier.

changes.change: New suspicious structural detector for literal-key encrypted-source concealment. Binds cipher receivers and plaintext variable across adjacent update/final/eval statements in one generator; accepts only the supported optional Promise delay shapes. Requires hex ciphertext and encoding, with no campaign-specific strings.

Preserve the original cipher-to-eval value-flow branch and add the anonymous-generator structural branch. Rename to describe both branches honestly; the old flow branch did not require literal keys or generators. Active registry-review expectations updated. Historical verification/evidence reports retain their historical IDs.

Remove unsupported install-hook/obfuscated-loader inference from a chosen basename plus any two generic source markers. Preserve the actually observed compact-source/one-long-line relationship as notable metadata, with its named-basename qualifier. Existing Function-construction, imports, line and whitespace primitives remain unchanged.

consumer_audit: No YAML exact consumers of either retired ID were found. Only the active registry-review cases referenced the renamed cipher rule; current references were updated.

Reviewed ancestor selectors for supply-chain/install-hook and hidden-payload, including Windsurf/MCP injection, package manifest, hidden listener, staged-loader and concealed-credential consumers. Removing formatting-only evidence intentionally stops it being an attack leg; actual loader and exfiltration evidence remains.

Before changing shared rules, inspected the existing registry generator/unrelated-eval fixtures, the zero-width npm execution fixture, and the bundled-preinstall VSIX credential-exfiltration fixture. Their actual attack detection remains.
No exclusion for Treasure Hunt or its provenance JSON was added. The dependency was independently fetched, verified, decoded and rescanned.

verification.matcher_cases: Eleven focused cases cover original and renamed bindings, both quote styles, optional/no delay, wrong cipher receiver, wrong eval variable, intervening overwrite, overwrite in yield, missing eval, dynamic key, and a benign compact numeric export.
verification.benign_shape_control: A data-only module.exports numeric array named preinstall.js receives the old suspicious loader finding under baseline rules. The corrected rules retain notable source-shape metadata and no hostile finding.
verification.retained_attacks: Compared complete per-unit hostile-ID sets for existing zero-width npm and bundled-preinstall VSIX fixtures. Both retain their hostile detections.
verification.reports: Full facts, baseline/final Atomscan reports, offline decrypted stages, upstream downloads/provenance and Cleave reports are retained under the named scratch directory.
verification.validation: Run make validate as the final action; final command result is recorded in the session.
verification.model_warning: Atomscan reports a v18 feature specification while this engine expects v21. Features added since that model version are absent from ML. YAML behavior findings are still present; no model files were changed.
verification.material_losses: No hostile-ID loss in the reviewed samples or retained attack fixtures. The two occurrences of the speculative preinstall/source-marker suspicion are intentionally replaced by precise notable metadata; new cipher-concealment suspicion keeps total suspicious occurrences unchanged on the loader.

scan_comparison.count_convention: Occurrences sum all analyzed units, including promoted findings, decoded children and fetch/dependency-verdict. Unique-ID counts are also recorded to avoid interpreting repeated propagation as distinct behavior.
